status: Proposed (2026-10-05) by openspec/changes/deck-pipeline, section 5a. Read by docs/mockups/lib/shipkit.js today and by deckc once it is built; the sizes are first choices judged on mockup screenshots, not measurements.
_rules: The detail a ship's decks are dressed with is generated from its layout by one rule set, so every room of a class reads alike and no room is decorated by hand (deck-pipeline section 5a; adapted from Undercity's tools/godot/detailing.py and its UT99 checklist, fps-game-demo f6cd25c).
Detail is not air: coves, ribs, beams and trims stand inside a compartment's brushes and the air model ignores them (life-support quotes brush volumes).

No z-fighting: every detail face is either pressed back to back against a wall, floor or ceiling (and not drawn), or stands at least 1 cm clear of any parallel face (CLAUDE.md section 8). Raised floor plates are raise_m above the floor for that reason.
Lengths in metres. A detail that would cross a portal opening is cut back to clear it; one that would be shorter than min_piece_m is dropped.

frames._doc: Ship frames: ribs on the walls and beams under the ceiling at fixed stations along the keel, frame k at z = origin_z_m + k * spacing_m. Walls that run fore and aft carry ribs at the frames; walls that run athwartships carry stiffeners at x = (k + 1/2) * spacing_m. A room taller than the cove's tall_room_m gets the deep beams and ribs.

cove._doc: A 45 degree panel between every solid wall and the ceiling: the hull's octagonal section, echoed inside. Not drawn along an edge open to another brush of the same compartment.

door_frame._doc: Every door, wall hatch and pressure door is framed: jambs and a lintel fill a ring cut around the clear opening (size_m stays the clear opening crew pass through), proud of the wall on each side. Pressure doors are heavier and hazard-striped. A status strip glows on the lintel.

floor_portal._doc: A hazard rim on the floor around every hatch, ladder well, hoist and bay door, and a trim collar under the ceiling around it. Ladders get rails and rungs from the lower floor to ladder_above_m over the upper one.

railing._doc: Along an edge where a brush opens onto a lower floor of the same compartment (a hangar gallery over the hangar floor): two rails, posts and a kick plate.

platforms._doc: Raised floors that are solid, not air (a dais, a work ring, a sub-platform; bridge-stations section 11a): a riser and a hazard nosing on every edge that is not against a wall, a railing on rail edges with gaps at stairs, treads of tread_rise_m.

kicks._doc: Kick lights (openspec/changes/kick-lights): indirect light at the foot of platform edges and consoles. platform: every edge of a kind in on is undercut at its foot by a recess height_m high and depth_m deep (the wall banks' own toe kick), a strip on a chamfer chamfer_m square at the back of the recess's ceiling, facing out and down. props: each console family's strips in prop space (props.json's frame: +Y up, +Z towards the operator, the origin on the floor at the centre of the back): y_m and z_m the strip's bottom and top edges (z at each), x_m its half width, x_inset_m in from the prop's bounds, or beside_m out from the bounds (a strip each side), normal the way it faces, type its fixture type (kick_strip unless named: column_strip for the light columns behind the terminals).

runner._doc: A deck plate strip down the middle of every corridor.

conduits._doc: Two pipes along the top of every fore-and-aft corridor wall, below the cove and clear of the ribs.

lamps._doc: The lamp rule (deck-pipeline section 5): lamps sit in the bays between frames, never on a beam. A bay gets round(area / area_per_lamp_m2) lamps across its width, a corridor bay at least one, a pod one. Every emergency_every-th lamp of a compartment is on the emergency bus. A room taller than tall_room_m gets high-bay lamps: radius and size scale with its height over 3 m, and they hang hang_m below the ceiling.

finishes._doc: Which material (data/materials/materials.json) each generated surface takes, by the compartment's finish in the layout.
